assignments.text:
To be
sure, it was not a man this time, but Miss Marjoribanks; but the
atmosphere thrilled and trembled to the advent of the new luminary all
the same.
assignments.summary: The narrator playfully reveals that the awaited transformative figure is not a man but Lucilla Marjoribanks, deflating grandiose revolutionary language through comic irony.
assignments.best_quote: To be sure, it was not a man this time, but Miss Marjoribanks; but the atmosphere thrilled and trembled to the advent of the new luminary all the same.

assignments.text:
There are people who talk of
themselves, and think of themselves, as it were, under protest, and with
depreciation, not actually able to convince themselves that anybody
cares; but Lucilla, for her part, had the calmest and most profound
conviction that, when she discussed her own doings and plans and
clevernesses, she was bringing forward the subject most interesting to
her audience as well as to herself. Such a conviction is never without
its fruits.
assignments.summary: Lucilla's complete conviction in her own importance is the source of her persuasiveness; she genuinely believes her interests are everyone's interests.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla, for her part, had the calmest and most profound conviction that, when she discussed her own doings and plans and clevernesses, she was bringing forward the subject most interesting to her audience as well as to herself

assignments.text:
Who could it be that possessed that voice
which Miss Marjoribanks felt by instinct was the very one thing
wanting—a round, full, delicious contralto, precisely adapted to
supplement without supplanting her own high-pitched and much-cultivated
organ? She stopped short before the door and made a rapid observation
even in the first moment of her surprise. The house was not exactly like
the other humble houses in Grove Street.
assignments.summary: Lucilla instinctively recognizes that this contralto voice is the perfect complement to her own soprano; it is the missing element for her social ambitions.
assignments.best_quote: Who could it be that possessed that voice which Miss Marjoribanks felt by instinct was the very one thing wanting—a round, full, delicious contralto, precisely adapted to supplement without supplanting her own high-pitched and much-cultivated organ?

assignments.text:
"And she has a nice little voice," Lucilla said to
herself, with the most friendly and tolerant feelings. Thus Miss
Marjoribanks prepared to establish her kingdom with a benevolence which
was almost Utopian, not upon the ruins of other thrones, but with the
goodwill and co-operation of the lesser powers, who were, to be sure,
too feeble to resist her advance, but whose rights she was quite ready
to recognise, and even to promote, in her own way.
assignments.summary: The narrator notes that Lucilla builds her kingdom benevolently, with the cooperation of lesser powers, not by destroying existing hierarchies but by co-opting them.
assignments.best_quote: Thus Miss Marjoribanks prepared to establish her kingdom with a benevolence which was almost Utopian, not upon the ruins of other thrones, but with the goodwill and co-operation of the lesser powers

assignments.text:
Dr
Marjoribanks's house could not have been better placed as a strategic
position, commanding as it did all Grange Lane, of which it was, so to
speak, the key, and yet affording a base of communication with the
profaner public, which Miss Marjoribanks was wise enough to know a
leader of society should never ignore completely; for, indeed, one of
the great advantages of that brilliant position is, that it gives a
woman a right to be arbitrary, and to select her materials according to
her judgment.
assignments.summary: The narrator observes that the Doctor's house commands Grange Lane geographically and socially, giving Lucilla strategic access to both elite and public society.
assignments.best_quote: Dr Marjoribanks's house could not have been better placed as a strategic position, commanding as it did all Grange Lane, of which it was, so to speak, the key

assignments.text:
She
knew, for example, that there was a great difference between the
brilliant society of London, or of Paris, which appears in books, where
women have generally the best of it, and can rule in their own right;
and even the very best society of a country town, where husbands are
very commonly unmanageable, and have a great deal more of their own way
in respect to the houses they will or will not go to, than is good for
that inferior branch of the human family.
assignments.summary: Lucilla understands that provincial society differs from metropolitan centers; in Carlingford, men control access to social spaces, so securing them through dining is the key to female influence.

assignments.text:
While every one else regarded the matter with, to some extent, a
personal bias, the only person who looked at it abstractly, and
contemplated not the accidents of an evening, but the work itself, which
was progressing in the face of all kinds of social difficulties, was the
master-mind which first conceived the grand design of turning the
chaotic elements of society in Carlingford into one grand unity.
assignments.summary: While others gossip about personal interests, Lucilla alone views the evening abstractly, focused on the progress of her grand design to organize Carlingford society.
assignments.best_quote: While every one else regarded the matter with, to some extent, a personal bias, the only person who looked at it abstractly, and contemplated not the accidents of an evening, but the work itself, which was progressing in the face of all kinds of social difficulties, was the master-mind which first conceived the grand design of turning the chaotic elements of society in Carlingford into one grand unity.

assignments.text:
When Dr
Marjoribanks had gone downstairs to resume the case which he was writing
out for the  Lancet , Lucilla passed through one of those moments of
sublime despondency which now and then try the spirits of the
benefactors of their race. A few tears came to her eyes as she reflected
upon this great problem. Without such trials genius would not fully know
itself nor be justly aware of its own strength.
assignments.summary: Lucilla is moved to tears as she contemplates the problem of her unbelieving followers; without trials genius would not know its own strength.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla passed through one of those moments of sublime despondency which now and then try the spirits of the benefactors of their race.

assignments.text:
When he raised his
head and looked round him, naturally Mr Beverley's eyes went direct to
the mark like an arrow; he looked, and he saw at the centre of the
table, surrounded by every kind of regard and consideration, full in the
light of the lamp, his favourite adventurer, the impostor whom he had
denounced the first time he took his place by Miss Marjoribanks's side.
assignments.summary: The Archdeacon's eyes are drawn directly to Mr Cavendish, exposed fully in the lamp's light at the table's centre—the moment of revelation.
assignments.best_quote: he looked, and he saw at the centre of the table, surrounded by every kind of regard and consideration, full in the light of the lamp, his favourite adventurer, the impostor whom he had denounced

assignments.text:
"A criminal? a conspirator?" said Mr Cavendish, and he looked in his
accuser's face with an amazement which, notwithstanding his rage, struck
the Archdeacon. If he had called him an impostor, the culprit would have
quailed and made no reply. But the exaggeration saved him. After that
first look of surprise, he rose to his feet and confronted the avenger,
who saw he had made a blunder without knowing what it was.
assignments.summary: Cavendish reacts with genuine surprise to being accused of crime and conspiracy, revealing that the Archdeacon has made a strategic error by exaggerating the charges.
assignments.best_quote: A criminal? a conspirator? said Mr Cavendish, and he looked in his accuser's face with an amazement which, notwithstanding his rage, struck the Archdeacon.

assignments.text:
He had been doing without them
for a week or two, and he had not liked it; and yet at that moment it
seemed to Mr Cavendish that he could rather be content to lose them all
at a stroke, to make it known in Carlingford that he was ruined and had
lost his fortune, than that Carlingford should find out that he was not,
after all, one of the Cavendishes, nor the person it took him for.
assignments.summary: Cavendish realizes he would rather be financially ruined than exposed as a fraud, revealing his desperate attachment to social position.
assignments.best_quote: he could rather be content to lose them all at a stroke, to make it known in Carlingford that he was ruined and had lost his fortune, than that Carlingford should find out that he was not, after all, one of the Cavendishes

assignments.text:
He
was there—he who had been so long away from Carlingford—he who had
been so deeply offended by hearing his name seriously coupled with that
of Barbara Lake—he who ought to have been anywhere in the world rather
than here upon the eve of his election, when all the world was keeping
watch over his conduct.
assignments.summary: Cavendish's presence in Barbara's parlour two days before the election represents a catastrophic breach of propriety and political judgment.
assignments.best_quote: He was there—he who had been so long away from Carlingford—he who had been so deeply offended by hearing his name seriously coupled with that of Barbara Lake—he who ought to have been anywhere in the world rather than here upon the eve of his election, when all the world was keeping watch over his conduct.

assignments.text:
Lucilla regarded him through
all these fluctuations with natural pity, and at the same time with the
calmness of a knowledge which was aware of all and had nothing more to
discover; and at the end Mr Cavendish perceived her calm, and the
absence of wonder and curiosity in her face, and began to perceive that
he had something very serious to deal with—more serious even than he
had at first supposed.
assignments.summary: Lucilla watches Cavendish's emotional swings with calm knowing, while he gradually realizes the gravity of the situation.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla regarded him through all these fluctuations with natural pity, and at the same time with the calmness of a knowledge which was aware of all and had nothing more to discover; and at the end Mr Cavendish perceived her calm, and the absence of wonder and curiosity in her face, and began to perceive that he had something very serious to deal with—more serious even than he had at first supposed.

assignments.text:
She took him off to his very face, and he never found it out, though
everybody else did, and the house shook with restrained laughter.
assignments.summary: Mrs Woodburn's mimicry is performed in the Archdeacon's presence, but he remains completely unaware while the company laughs in barely restrained hilarity.
assignments.best_quote: She took him off to his very face, and he never found it out, though everybody else did, and the house shook with restrained laughter.

assignments.text:
Whether it
was that little speech of hers which touched the mimic's heart, or
whether the effect was produced by some other secret influence, it is
certain that this was the night on which Mrs Woodburn's talent came to
what may be called a sort of apotheosis. She shook off her languor as by
a sudden inspiration, and gave such a sketch of the Archdeacon as up to
this day is remembered more clearly in Carlingford than the man himself.
assignments.summary: Mrs Woodburn suddenly recovers her powers and delivers a brilliant mimicry of the Archdeacon that becomes legendary in Carlingford.
assignments.best_quote: She shook off her languor as by a sudden inspiration, and gave such a sketch of the Archdeacon as up to this day is remembered more clearly in Carlingford than the man himself.

assignments.text:
The mimic was a little indolent, and would not take the trouble
to make any exertions for the good of the community, except in the
exercise of her peculiar talent, though she had been known, when
excited, to go through real fatigue for that; but she had none of the
steady force, the persevering energy—or, to sum up all in one word, the
genius—of Miss Marjoribanks, who, for her part, recognised the  use  of
such an instrument of entertainment as Mrs Woodburn possessed without
appreciating it in her own person; for Lucilla had no sense of humour,
as she candidly admitted, with that consciousness of her own faults, and
slight disposition to consider them virtues, which is common to persons
of great endowments.
assignments.summary: The narrator elaborates the fundamental difference: Mrs Woodburn relies on mimicry and entertainment talent, while Lucilla possesses steady organisational force, though Lucilla lacks humour despite her other gifts.
assignments.best_quote: Lucilla had no sense of humour, as she candidly admitted, with that consciousness of her own faults, and slight disposition to consider them virtues, which is common to persons of great endowments.

assignments.text:
Of course, there will be a party that will get
up a memorial, and prove that a man so kind-hearted never existed out of
paradise; and there will be another party who will prove him to be
insane; and then at the end all the blackguards within a hundred miles
will crowd into Carlingford, and the fellow will be hanged, as he
deserves to be; but I assure you it's a famous amusement for a country
town."
assignments.summary: The barrister elaborates that executions provide entertainment, with predictable memorials, insanity defences, and crowds of criminals attending.
assignments.best_quote: it's a famous amusement for a country town.

assignments.text:
When Lucilla had shed
these few tears over her subjects' weakness and want of faith, she rose
up again in new strength from the momentary downfall. It was, as we have
said, a sublime moment. The idea of giving them up, and leaving their
affairs to their own guidance, never for an instant penetrated into her
heroic mind; but she was human, and naturally she felt the prick of
ingratitude.
assignments.summary: Lucilla rises from despair with renewed commitment to her causes; her heroism lies in persisting despite ingratitude.
assignments.best_quote: The idea of giving them up, and leaving their affairs to their own guidance, never for an instant penetrated into her heroic mind; but she was human, and naturally she felt the prick of ingratitude.

assignments.text:
Her
instinct, even when reason suggested that she should be doubtful of
them, was always to side with her own friends; and though there might be
persons included in that sacred number who were scarcely worthy of the
character, yet Lucilla, like every lofty character, could act but
according to her own nature, and could not forsake any one whom she
supposed to be thus mysteriously and darkly assailed.
assignments.summary: Lucilla's instinct is always to protect her friends, even against reason; her nature compels her loyalty regardless of their worthiness.
assignments.best_quote: Her instinct, even when reason suggested that she should be doubtful of them, was always to side with her own friends; and though there might be persons included in that sacred number who were scarcely worthy of the character, yet Lucilla, like every lofty character, could act but according to her own nature, and could not forsake any one whom she supposed to be thus mysteriously and darkly assailed.

assignments.text:
She had
no vocation, such as the foundress of such an establishment ought to
have, nor did she see her way to the abandonment of all projects for
herself, and that utter devotion to the cause of humanity which would be
involved in it; but yet, when a woman happens to be full of energy and
spirit, and determined that whatever she may be she shall certainly not
be a nonentity, her position is one that demands thought.
assignments.summary: Lucilla lacks true religious vocation but will not surrender personal ambition; her energetic temperament creates an unresolved ethical dilemma.
assignments.best_quote: but yet, when a woman happens to be full of energy and spirit, and determined that whatever she may be she shall certainly not be a nonentity, her position is one that demands thought

assignments.text:
People who know no better may go
away upon marriage tours, or they may fly off to foreign travel, or go
out as governesses, when all things do not go just as they wish. But as
for Miss Marjoribanks, she stood bravely at her post, and scorned to
flinch or run away. Thus commenced, amid mists of discouragement, and in
an entire absence of all that was calculated to stimulate and
exhilarate, the second grand period of Lucilla's life.
assignments.summary: While lesser people flee through marriage, travel, or governessing when disappointed, Lucilla stands firm at her post and begins her second campaign amid discouragement and without support.
assignments.best_quote: But as for Miss Marjoribanks, she stood bravely at her post, and scorned to flinch or run away. Thus commenced, amid mists of discouragement, and in an entire absence of all that was calculated to stimulate and exhilarate, the second grand period of Lucilla's life.

assignments.text:
She even had the strength to get up to meet him, and hold
out her hands to him by way of welcome—but found herself, before she
knew how, in the arms of a man with a beard, who was so much changed in
his own person that he ventured to kiss her, which was a thing Tom
Marjoribanks, though her cousin, had never dared to do before.
assignments.summary: Lucilla rises to greet Tom but finds herself embraced by a bearded, transformed man who dares to kiss her.
assignments.best_quote: she found herself, before she knew how, in the arms of a man with a beard, who was so much changed in his own person that he ventured to kiss her, which was a thing Tom Marjoribanks, though her cousin, had never dared to do before.

assignments.text:
"Lucilla," said Tom Marjoribanks, "you know I always had a great regard
for my uncle. But it was not for him I came back. He was never half so
fond of me as I am of you. You know that as well as I do. There never
was a time that I would not have gone to the other end of the world if
you had told me; and I have done it as near as possible.
assignments.summary: Tom declares his deep regard for Lucilla has always exceeded his regard for her father, and that he left for India at her behest.
assignments.best_quote: There never was a time that I would not have gone to the other end of the world if you had told me; and I have done it as near as possible.

assignments.text:
We mention this fact rather as a contribution to the
history of those phenomena of the human mind, which have as yet escaped
the metaphysician, than as an actual circumstance in the life of Miss
Marjoribanks. She was a woman of genius, and he only a very simple,
unlucky fellow; and yet a sensation of comfort came to Lucilla's heart
when she said "Poor Tom!"
assignments.summary: The narrator remarks that this psychological phenomenon—genius finding comfort in simple faith—is remarkable and deserves attention.
assignments.best_quote: She was a woman of genius, and he only a very simple, unlucky fellow; and yet a sensation of comfort came to Lucilla's heart when she said 'Poor Tom!'

assignments.text:
It was natural, and indeed it was only proper, that Miss Marjoribanks
should cry—which she did abundantly, partly for grief, and partly
because of the flutter of agitation, and something like joy, in which
she was, and which, considering that she had always frankly owned that
she was fond of Tom, was quite natural too.
assignments.summary: Lucilla cries abundantly, partly from grief over her father and partly from emotional agitation and unexpected joy at Tom's presence.
assignments.best_quote: partly for grief, and partly because of the flutter of agitation, and something like joy

assignments.text:
And then he went out
to discover, if possible, what was coming to him. The difference was,
that in this battle no honour, but only a possible salvage of reputation
and fortunate escape, was to be gained.
assignments.summary: Cavendish ventures out to face his crisis, understanding that he fights not for glory but for mere survival and the salvaging of his reputation.
assignments.best_quote: In this battle no honour, but only a possible salvage of reputation and fortunate escape, was to be gained.

assignments.text:
When he was
coming out of the house, as a matter of course, he met with the chief of
his Dissenting supporters, accompanied (for Mr Bury, as has been said,
was very Low-Church, and loved, wherever he could do it, to work in
unison with his Dissenting brethren) by the Rector's churchwarden, both
of whom stopped with a curiously critical air to speak to the Candidate,
who had to be every man's friend for the time being.
assignments.summary: Cavendish encounters his key supporters leaving the Lake house, and their critical looks suggest they have observed and judged his visit.
assignments.best_quote: When he was coming out of the house, as a matter of course, he met with the chief of his Dissenting supporters, accompanied (for Mr Bury, as has been said, was very Low-Church, and loved, wherever he could do it, to work in unison with his Dissenting brethren) by the Rector's churchwarden, both of whom stopped with a curiously critical air to speak to the Candidate

assignments.text:
This had been a comfort
to his mind, but it was the very falsest and most deceitful consolation. That intervening Sunday was a severer calamity for Mr Cavendish than
half a dozen ordinary days. The general excitement had risen so high,
and all the chances on both sides had been so often discussed and
debated, that something new was as water in the desert to the thirsting
constituency.
assignments.summary: The heightened election excitement makes Sunday a worse day for secrecy than any ordinary day; the news spreads like water in a desert.
assignments.best_quote: That intervening Sunday was a severer calamity for Mr Cavendish than half a dozen ordinary days.

assignments.text:
And it was not even the scriptural coals of fire she was
thinking of as she pondered her great undertaking in her mind. The
enterprise might not be free from a touch of human vanity, but it was
vanity of a loftier description: the pleasure of exercising a great
faculty, and the natural confidence of genius in its own powers.
assignments.summary: Lucilla's motivation is not even malicious revenge but rather a noble vanity—the pleasure of exercising her great talents and the confidence of genius in its own powers.
assignments.best_quote: And it was not even the scriptural coals of fire she was thinking of as she pondered her great undertaking in her mind. The enterprise might not be free from a touch of human vanity, but it was vanity of a loftier description: the pleasure of exercising a great faculty, and the natural confidence of genius in its own powers.

assignments.text:
We have recorded her beginning in all the fulness of youthful confidence
and undaunted trust in her own resources; and have done our best to show
that in the course of organising society Miss Marjoribanks, like all
other benefactors of their kind, had many sacrifices to make, and had to
undergo the mortification of finding out that many of her most able
efforts turned to other people's profit and went directly against
herself.
assignments.summary: The narrator reviews Lucilla's initial confidence and early achievements in organizing Carlingford society, while noting the ironic cost of her efforts.
assignments.best_quote: like all other benefactors of their kind, had many sacrifices to make, and had to undergo the mortification of finding out that many of her most able efforts turned to other people's profit

assignments.text:
People who like to discover the alloy which blends
with all human motives, may suppose that Lucilla felt her own credit as
the leader of society at stake, and would not admit that she had been
duped. But this had in reality but a very small share in the matter.
assignments.summary: While others might suppose Lucilla's self-interest drives her actions, Oliphant asserts that reputation concerns play only a minor role in her character.
assignments.best_quote: People who like to discover the alloy which blends with all human motives, may suppose that Lucilla felt her own credit as the leader of society at stake, and would not admit that she had been duped. But this had in reality but a very small share in the matter.
